# A two-limb number from a value of T

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `make_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

The two-limb number with the value $a$, exactly:

$$x = a.$$

## C++

**Not yet called by the public headers.** No public operation computes this kernel yet.

## Requires

- $a$ is any value of `T`: a number, $\pm\infty$ or a NaN.

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- $x$ is canonical and is $a$ exactly: when $a$ is finite, $x$ is finite and normalized with $x_0 + x_1 = a$; when $a = \pm\infty$, $x = (\pm\infty, 0)$; when $a$ is a NaN, $x = (\mathrm{NaN}, \mathrm{NaN})$.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `make_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeMake.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeMake.v); `make -C proofs` finds no axiom in its proof beyond the four allowed ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md)).

## Source

**Algorithm:** constructors (Milestone 1 listing). **License:** algorithm: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/make_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/make_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# Expansion<T, 2> from a value of T or from a one-limb number: (a, 0), canonical. The guard makes
# a value the program may have computed as a product into a number the compiler cannot fuse
# (rule R3); a NaN gives (NaN, NaN), an infinity (inf, 0) (milestone1.md, "Values that enter from
# the program").

x0 = guard(a)
n  = eq(x0, x0)
x1 = select(n, 0, x0)
```

No stored brute-force run has judged this kernel yet.

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
